draft.title: Limitation of actions
card: A limitation period is the time limit for starting a civil claim. It is set by law, in Victoria mainly by the Limitation of Actions Act 1958 (Vic).
The length depends on the type of claim. Many claims, such as those in contract, have a period of six years.

The period usually runs from the day the cause of action arises, for example when the breach of contract happens. If the plaintiff files after it ends, the defendant can raise the time limit as a defence and the claim can be lost.
Time limits keep evidence fresh and give defendants certainty that old disputes will not suddenly return. Some situations, such as claims by children, have different rules.
draft.remember: A civil claim must be started within the time the law allows, or it can be lost.

a.q: Why does the law set limitation periods for civil claims?
opts: So claims are brought while evidence is still fresh
So defendants never have to pay for any harm they cause
So only claims about contracts can reach a court
So plaintiffs must prove their case more strongly
a.why: Over time witnesses forget and documents are lost, so a time limit helps keep evidence reliable and gives defendants certainty. It does not remove liability for harm brought in time, and it does not change how strongly a plaintiff must prove the case.
a.clue: Think about what happens to witnesses and records as years pass.

b.q: Sam's builder breached their contract in 2015. Sam files a claim in 2024, nine years later, where the period is six years. What is the likely result?
opts: The claim can be lost because it was filed too late
The claim succeeds because the breach really happened
The claim succeeds only if Sam proves loss on the balance
The claim is moved to a criminal court instead
b.why: The six-year period ended before Sam filed, so the defendant can use the time limit as a defence and the claim can be lost. It does not matter that the breach really happened, because the time limit is a separate bar to the claim.
b.clue: Count the years between the breach and the filing.

a.best: So claims are brought while evidence is still fresh

b.best: The claim can be lost because it was filed too late

problems.detail: The distractor 'The claim succeeds only if Sam proves loss on the balance' cuts off 'balance of probabilities'. The shortened phrase may confuse students, and it leans on ideas from points 2 and 3.
